guide.title: CCConfig · Node.js required
guide.heading: Node.js is required
guide.subtitle: CCConfig desktop reuses your installed Node.js to run its local service. It does not bundle a runtime.
guide.headingStartupFailed: The local service did not start
guide.subtitleStartupFailed: CCConfig desktop needs a background Node service, and it failed to start this time. The reason is shown below.
guide.installDownloadPrefix: Or download from the official site:
guide.installRequirement: Requires >= 18. After installing, fully quit and reopen CCConfig.
guide.pathTitle: Already installed Node.js but still seeing this page?
guide.pathDesc: Apps launched from Finder/Dock do not inherit your terminal PATH, so Node.js managed by nvm / fnm / volta is often not detected. You can point CCConfig at it explicitly:
guide.pathDescWin: The Windows build checks Program Files, nvm-windows, fnm, volta and PATH automatically. If it still cannot find Node.js, point it at node.exe in PowerShell:
guide.pathComment1: # 1. Find the node binary in your terminal
guide.pathComment2: # 2. Restart the app with the environment variable
guide.pathComment2Win: # 2. Persist the user env var, then fully quit and reopen CCConfig
guide.pathLaunchctlDesc: You can also set a global launchctl variable so Dock launches work:
guide.troubleshootDesc: Startup logs are written to ~/.ccconfig/logs/sidecar.log, including every Node.js path that was tried.
guide.troubleshootDescWin: Startup logs are written to %USERPROFILE%\.ccconfig\logs\sidecar.log, including every Node.js path that was tried.
